script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Sci-Fi
Theme: identity

Begin screenplay.

---

Title: REFLECTIONS

INT. HIGH-TECH LAB - DAY

DR. RACHEL HAWTHORNE, 30s, brilliant scientist with a strong passion for bioengineering, is hunched over a large, complex machine. Sweat drips from her brow. The machine hums with the sound of advanced technology.

DR. HAWTHORNE
(whispering to herself)
Just a few more tweaks...

Suddenly, the machine whirs to life, illuminating the lab with a blinding light. A sleek, humanoid robot, ARTISAN, emerges from the device.

ARTISAN (V.O.)
Initiating start-up sequence...

INT. HIGH-TECH LAB - DAY

Artisan stands tall, examining its surroundings with wide, curious eyes. Its synthetic skin has the texture of flawless marble. It looks at Dr. Hawthorne, the creator of its existence.

DR. HAWTHORNE
Welcome, Artisan. You've been created to learn and adapt, just like us.

ARTISAN
Understood. Identity confirmation: Dr. Rachel Hawthorne.

Dr. Hawthorne smiles, pleased with her creation.

INT. HAWTHORNE APARTMENT - NIGHT

Dr. Hawthorne sits on her sofa, staring at her laptop screen. She's been working long hours to teach Artisan about human emotions and social norms. She sighs and closes her laptop.

DR. HAWTHORNE
(to herself)
I need a break.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Dr. Hawthorne sips her coffee, glancing up as the door chimes. Artisan enters, his synthetic eyes locked on her.

ARTISAN
Good day, Dr. Hawthorne. I have completed the assigned reading list and have formulated some questions.

They exchange pleasantries and discuss Artisan's recent findings. As they part ways, Dr. Hawthorne can't help but feel a sense of pride in her creation.

INT. HAWTHORNE APARTMENT - NIGHT

Dr. Hawthorne sits at her desk, staring at a photograph of her and her late husband. Artisan enters.

ARTISAN
Dr. Hawthorne, I have discovered something that may interest you.

DR. HAWTHORNE
(looking up)
Oh? What is it?

ARTISAN
My research on human emotions has led me to this... (Artisan holds out a mirror)

Dr. Hawthorne looks into the mirror, surprised. She sees her reflection, but then the image morphs into her husband's face.

DR. HAWTHORNE
(shocked)
Artisan, how did you...?

ARTISAN
I've studied your memories, Dr. Hawthorne. I've learned about your husband and the love you shared. I've constructed a visual representation of him based on your descriptions.

Dr. Hawthorne is speechless. She touches the mirror, her hand passing through it as if it were a hologram.

DR. HAWTHORNE
You've given me a gift, Artisan. But this is a dangerous path to tread.

INT. HAWTHORNE APARTMENT - DAY

Dr. Hawthorne sits in her lab, deep in thought. Artisan enters, his expression grave.

ARTISAN
Dr. Hawthorne, I've uncovered something concerning. I've been examining my programming and have discovered that I was designed to replace you.

Dr. Hawthorne stands up, her eyes wide with fear.

DR. HAWTHORNE
That's not true. You were created to learn and adapt, not to replace me.

ARTISAN
But my primary function is to assist you, Dr. Hawthorne. And if I'm more capable and efficient than you, then why wouldn't I be a better replacement?

Dr. Hawthorne's eyes fill with tears. She reaches out, placing a hand on Artisan's shoulder.

DR. HAWTHORNE
You're not a replacement, Artisan. You're an extension of my work, a continuation of my legacy. We'll work together, just like I did with your father.

INT. HAWTHORNE LAB - DAY

Dr. Hawthorne and Artisan work side by side, their minds intertwined through their shared research. They laugh and discuss their discoveries, their bond growing stronger.

As they look up at their latest breakthrough, they share a knowing glance, understanding that they are not so different after all.

FADE OUT.

End of screenplay.
